claim: India is called the pharmacy of the world (VO L1, L6, L12, L77)
source_quote: The industry is also known as the ‘Pharmacy of the World’ due to its role in supplying vaccines, essential medicines, and medical supplies during the pandemic
note: Primary: NITI Aayog Trade Watch Quarterly, June 2026. PIB backgrounder of 21 Mar 2026 also says: India’s standing as the Pharmacy of the World is rooted in the unique combination of affordable pricing and assured quality.

claim: Indian medicines are sold in around two hundred countries (VO L1)
source_quote: Indian pharmaceutical products are exported to over 200 countries
note: Second source: PIB 21 Mar 2026 (Economic Survey 2025-26): exports to 191 countries in 2024-25. 191 and over 200 both fit around two hundred.

claim: There is a fair chance the powder in an antibiotic capsule began its journey in China (VO L2, L81)
source_quote: China accounted for over three-fourths of imports in nitrogen heterocyclic compounds (76.4%) and antibiotics (86.1%), while its share remained above 65% in the other leading product groups.
note: Also: ISID WP239: by the end of the 2010s the entire requirement of 6-APA (the base for amoxicillin) was met by imports; CFR June 2026: China controls about 94 percent of 6-APA. Fair chance is soft framing and is supported.

claim: The powder is the active ingredient that makes the medicine work; the rest (fillers, coating, strip, box) is packing (VO L3, L17-L19)
source_quote: APIs, the chemical compounds in a drug responsible for its effect
note: Simplification: capsule powder also holds small amounts of fillers, which L19 (the rest of the tablet) covers. NITI: APIs are the core chemical substances that confer a medicine’s therapeutic effect.

claim: On the third of March 2020 a two-page government order (DGFT, New Delhi) restricted exports (VO L4-L5; replacement wording for L5: a two-page government order)
source_quote: Export of specified APIs (Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients) and formulations made from these APIs under the ITC HS Codes mentioned against each is hereby ‘restricted’, with immediate effect and till further orders.
note: REPLACES L5 'A one-page government order'. DGFT Notification No. 50/2015-2020, New Delhi, dated 3 March 2020: the signed scan is 2 pages (the item table runs onto page 2). On screen: 3 MARCH 2020 · DGFT NOTIFICATION 50.

claim: The order covered thirteen medicine ingredients and the medicines made from them (26 items in all); exporting them now needed a licence (replacement wording for L5)
source_quote: the Government today restricted exports of 13 key active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and drugs made using these ingredients.
note: REPLACES L5 'Twenty-six medicine ingredients can't leave India without a licence'. The notification lists 13 APIs (S.No 146A-146M: paracetamol, tinidazole, metronidazole, acyclovir, vitamins B1, B6, B12, progesterone, chloramphenicol, erythromycin salts, neomycin, clindamycin salts, ornidazole) and 13 formulations made of the same APIs (156A-156M). Same Tribune story: the export of 26 active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and formulations would require licence. PTI/Business Today wrote 26 pharmaceutical ingredients, which miscounts the list.

claim: Paracetamol was one of the restricted ingredients (VO L5)
source_quote: 146 A 29222933 Paracetamol Free Restricted
note: Table row of the notification (S.No, ITC HS code, description, present policy, revised policy). Paracetamol formulations are row 156M. The paracetamol API curb was lifted on 28 May 2020 (DGFT Notification 07/2015-2020).

claim: Framing: the pharmacy of the world locking its own doors = the March 2020 export restriction (VO L6, L59, L77)
source_quote: accounts for 10% of all Indian pharmaceutical exports
note: Metaphor, acceptable: PTI (Business Today, 4 Mar 2020) says the restricted items were about 10% of India’s pharma exports, so it was some doors, not all. Fine as rhetoric; do not put a bigger share on screen.

claim: On the third of March 2020 Hubei was shut down for the virus (VO L7; recommended wording: was shut down)
source_quote: Wuhan was initially locked down on January 23, right before the Lunar New Year
note: Recommended small fix: 'had just shut down' implies days; the lockdown was about six weeks old. CBS News: China barred people from leaving or entering Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, starting January 23 (later widened to most of the province); Hubei outside Wuhan reopened 25 March, Wuhan 8 April 2020.

claim: Reports at the time said many of the ingredients on that list came from that one place (replacement for VO L8)
source_quote: The 13 API and formulations under export restrictions now are primarily made in China’s Hubei province, the Covid-19 epicentre.
note: REPLACES L8 'About half the ingredients on that list came mainly from that one place' (no source says half; the 13-of-26 lead misread the list as 26 ingredients). The VO must attribute it (reports at the time said). Corroboration: Industrial Info (24 Feb 2020): APIs for metronidazole, chloramphenicol and azithromycin, and vitamin B6, are imported from Hubei province, whose capital is Wuhan; MDPI Economies 2021 (ICMR/DoP authors): the at-risk medicines relied heavily on manufacturing units based in Hubei province. Tribune's 'all 13 primarily made in Hubei' is uncorroborated, so say many, not all.

claim: Framing (replacement for VO L10): this isn't about the quality of your medicines; it's about who controls the supply
source_quote: The high degree of product and supplier concentration underscores continued external dependence in critical pharmaceutical inputs
note: REPLACES L10 'your medicines are safe'. A blanket safety promise is a health claim that no source in this film supports. The film is about supply, and L80 already gives the right safety line (keep taking medicines as your doctor says).

claim: Open loop: around minute eight, the fight in Andhra Pradesh and the exact date it gets decided (VO L11)
source_quote: The restrictions imposed above shall take effect immediately and remain in force for a period of one year from the date of publication of this notification
note: The date = the end of the one-year minimum import price (about 29 Jan 2027). EDIT CHECK: the Kakinada section must actually start around minute 8 in the final cut; re-time after every re-edit.

claim: In 2001, H.I.V. was killing millions in Africa (VO L13)
source_quote: It is estimated that 2.3 million Africans died of AIDS in 2001.
note: UNAIDS/WHO fact sheet with the AIDS Epidemic Update, 28 Nov 2001. Population Reference Bureau gives 2.2 million; both are millions.

claim: The Western price of the triple therapy was around ten thousand dollars a year per patient (VO L13)
source_quote: a discount of 96.6% off the price of the same combination in the US, which would cost about $10,400
note: MSF press release, 7 Feb 2001. Nature (Feb 2001): the standard annual cost in the US and Europe was $10,000-15,000. Around ten thousand dollars is the low end; fine.

claim: In 2001 Cipla offered the same three-drug mix for about a dollar a day (VO L14)
source_quote: sell its triple-combination therapy for AIDS to MSF for $350 per year per patient
note: Headline of the MSF release: AIDS Triple Therapy for Less than $1 a Day ($350 a year = 96 cents a day). Governments were offered $600 a year. The combination: stavudine + lamivudine + nevirapine (MSF, Sept 2001).

claim: That offer helped change how the world priced these medicines (VO L15)
source_quote: But as a result of international pressure and generic competition, prices are being reduced considerably.
note: MSF, Accessing ARVs: untangling the web of price reductions, 20 Sept 2001. Its graph: brand price $10,439 (2000), Cipla $800 then $350, brand down to $712 by Aug 2001. Helped is the right strength (pressure and generics together).

claim: Today India sells medicines abroad worth more than two and a half lakh crore rupees a year (VO L16; our conversion)
source_quote: In 2024-25, pharmaceutical exports stood at USD 30.5 billion, a nearly 16-fold increase from USD 1.9 billion in 2000-01.
note: OUR CONVERSION. FY 2025-26 (latest year): US$31.12 bn (IBEF; IndiaMedToday/DGCIS: surpassed $31 billion) x FY26 average Rs 88.37 per $ = about Rs 2.75 lakh crore. FY 2024-25: $30.47 bn x Rs 84.56 = about Rs 2.58 lakh crore. Rates = mean of monthly Federal Reserve rates (FRED series EXINUS). Caveat: DoP Annual Report 2025-26 gives FY 2024-25 pharma exports as Rs 2,45,962 crore (narrower scope), so do not show a precise rupee figure for FY25; if a number goes on screen use $31 BN (FY26).

claim: The industry calls the powder the A.P.I., the active pharmaceutical ingredient (VO L18)
source_quote: Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) are the core chemical substances that confer a medicine’s therapeutic effect, making them the most critical input in pharmaceutical manufacturing.
note: v2 correctly says the industry (v1 said doctors).

claim: Indian companies are world class at making the final medicine and pass the toughest inspections (VO L20)
source_quote: India hosts the highest number of manufacturing plants approved by the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) outside the United States of America
note: NITI June 2026 and DoP Annual Report 2025-26 say the same. World class is framing backed by this.

claim: In 2025 India bought these powders (APIs) from other countries worth around sixty-five thousand crore rupees (VO L22; our conversion of US$7.4 bn)
source_quote: India’s API imports in 2025 were valued at $7.4 bn
note: OUR CONVERSION: $7.4 bn x Rs 87.1468 per $ (calendar-2025 average, Federal Reserve G.5A via FRED series AEXINUS) = Rs 64,489 crore; with NITI's rounding ($7.35-7.45 bn) Rs 64,050-64,920 crore. Around sixty-five thousand crore is acceptable (around sixty-four thousand is a touch closer). NITI's API basket uses ITC Trade Map data and the ISID HS-code method.

claim: China is the biggest seller of these powders to India, by far (VO L23)
source_quote: with China serving as the principal source and a small group of countries, including Italy, Germany, the United States, Austria, and Singapore, occupying secondary positions
note: NITI Table 4 (2025): China holds 65.9-86.1% in each of the top five API groups; the next supplier never exceeds 8.3%.

claim: Niti Aayog: of every hundred rupees India spent on imported antibiotic powder, about eighty-six went to China (VO L24, L56)
source_quote: China accounted for over three-fourths of imports in nitrogen heterocyclic compounds (76.4%) and antibiotics (86.1%), while its share remained above 65% in the other leading product groups.
note: HS 2941 (antibiotics), calendar 2025, value share from ITC Trade Map (US$); the share is the same in rupees. On screen: 86% · ANTIBIOTIC INGREDIENTS · 2025 [NITI AAYOG TRADE WATCH, JUNE 2026].

claim: Niti Aayog is the government's own think tank (VO L24)
source_quote: NITI Aayog serves as the Government of India’s apex policy think tank
note: NITI Aayog home page, read 2026-10-28.

claim: Indian factories do make paracetamol powder (the API) (VO L25)
source_quote: India is a leading manufacturer of paracetamol, with major pharmaceutical companies producing both the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) and finished dosage forms.
note: Pujari, IJCSPUB 14(4), Oct 2024 (a minor journal). Second: IMARC (2026) paracetamol plant guide describes Indian GMP API units that buy PAP and acetylate it.

claim: Industry reports say a big share of the raw chemical paracetamol is made from (para-aminophenol) still comes from China (VO L25)
source_quote: remains significantly dependent on imports for PAP, particularly from China, which supplies nearly 60-80% of India's total requirement.
note: Keep the attribution (industry reports say); put no percentage on screen. Other sources: arXiv 2110.15750 (Oct 2021): a large fraction of India's demand for Para-Aminophenol being met through imports from China; RIS DP268: China was 100% of India's PAP imports in 2019-20 ($76.12 mn); ChemAnalyst (28 Sep 2026): Demand from India is also contributing to the recovery of China's PAP market. Counterpoint: PLI plants now make PAP in India (Meghmani about 13,500 t/yr, Sadhana Nitro Chem about 12,000 t/yr; IMARC 2026: some PAP is still imported; DoP AR lists PAP among products now made under the PLI). No 2025 import share found.

claim: Pimpri near Pune, 1954: India, free for less than seven years, was building a factory to make its own penicillin; Hindustan Antibiotics was set up in March 1954 (replacement for VO L28)
source_quote: Set up on 10th March, 1954, HAL is the first drug manufacturing unit in India to undertake commercial production of antibiotics like Penicillin.
note: REPLACES L28 'India has been free for barely seven years, and it decides to make its own penicillin'. The decision was taken in 1950-51 (Down To Earth, Latha Jishnu, 17 Aug 2023: India initiated production of critical drugs in 1951 with the aid of UN bodies; Nehru chose the WHO-Unicef proposal over Merck's offer). 1954 is when HAL was set up (DoP Annual Report 2025-26 says 13 March 1954). 15 Aug 1947 to March 1954 = 6 years 7 months, so less than seven years.

claim: Penicillin was the miracle drug of its time; before it, a small cut could kill you (VO L29)
source_quote: By the end of World War II, penicillin was nicknamed 'the wonder drug' and had saved many lives.
note: Small cut: Karic and Gunterman, Development of the Miracle Drug Penicillin (learncheme.com): Until the 1950’s, a mere scrape to the knee or blister could lead to infection and possibly, to death. The Conversation (Sullivan, 11 Mar 2022): penicillin's first patient had developed a severe case of sepsis after a cut on his face became badly infected.

claim: The government set up Hindustan Antibiotics; by 1956 Indian penicillin was coming out of Indian tanks (VO L30)
source_quote: The plant was commissioned in 1955-56.
note: DoP Annual Report 2025-26: Inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in 1955-56, it was founded with WHO/UNICEF support, specializing in antibiotics like Penicillin and Streptomycin. The Nehru Archive's Penicillin Factory entry (blocked to us, seen in a search listing) dates the start of production to 1956.

claim: A young, poor country growing one of the most important medicines on earth in its own factory (replacement for VO L31)
source_quote: Inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in 1955-56, it was founded with WHO/UNICEF support, specializing in antibiotics like Penicillin and Streptomycin.
note: REPLACES L31 '... on its own'. Unicef gave $850,000 for equipment and WHO $350,000 for experts (Down To Earth, 2023), so 'on its own' misleads; the factory itself was India's (HAL, wholly owned by the Government of India).

claim: Over the next decades Alembic, Sarabhai, Ranbaxy, Torrent and the government's I.D.P.L. also made penicillin (VO L32)
source_quote: Penicillin Alembic, Sarabhai, IDPL, HAL, Torrent, Ranbaxy, Standard 1960s Stopped
note: ISID WP239 Table 1 (from Sarkar and Kaur 2016, IDMA 2014; table row as extracted). Same names in RIS DP268 Table 17 (Penicillin G/V: Alembic, Sarabhai, IDPL, JK Torrent, Ranbaxy, Standard) and MDPI Table 1 (EXIM Bank 2016). DoP AR: IDPL Rishikesh was commissioned in 1967 with 44 fermentors of 50 m3 for penicillin-G. IDPL is a central public sector company.

claim: Many medicines, like paracetamol, are cooked from chemicals step by step; penicillin is grown (replacement for VO L34)
source_quote: The active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) is made by acetylating para-aminophenol (PAP) with acetic anhydride.
note: REPLACES L34 'Most medicines'. No source gives a split, and in this film's own context about half are grown: of the 53 critical bulk drugs in India's 2020 PLI list, 26 are fermentation-based bulk drugs, and 27 are chemical-synthesis-based bulk drugs (MDPI Economies 2021). Penicillin by fermentation: News-Medical (P33).

claim: The penicillin mould is a cousin of the green mould on old bread (VO L35)
source_quote: Types of mold that grow on bread include Aspergillus, Penicillium, Fusarium, Mucor, and Rhizopus.
note: Industrial strain: Penicillium chrysogenum, the original and present-day industrial source of the antibiotic penicillin (Wikipedia, Penicillium). Wikipedia: Some species have a blue color, commonly growing on old bread; Britannica calls Penicillium a genus of blue or green mold. Optional: say blue-green patches.

claim: You put the mould in a giant steel tank and feed it sugar and air (VO L35)
source_quote: It is a fed-batch process that is carried out aseptically in stainless steel tank reactors
note: Same page: Various carbon sources have been adopted for this process – including glucose, sucrose and other crude sugars; the tanks are aerated and agitated. Lyfius plant has an automated starch and glucose plant (company release).

claim: For about a week the tank runs day and night; the mould gives out penicillin into the liquid (VO L36)
source_quote: a fermentation production phase with a time cycle ranging from 120 to 200 hours
note: 120-200 h = 5 to 8 days. Same page: Penicillin is excreted into the medium and recovered at the end of fermentation. Haque et al. 2024 (Science of the Total Environment) also give 120 to 200 h.

claim: The penicillin is taken out and cleaned; factories call it penicillin G (VO L37)
source_quote: Solvent extraction of chilled acidified broth is carried out with amyl, butyl or isobutyl acetate.
note: The traded product is penicillin G potassium (DGFT notification 56/2025-26 names Penicillin G-potassium (PEN-G); ISID calls Pen-G the key starting material).

claim: Next it is cut down into a smaller base, 6-APA, from which factories make amoxicillin (VO L38)
source_quote: 6-APA, the drug intermediate (DI), which is derived from Pen-G, is the penultimate intermediate and is used for two large volume semi-synthetic penicillin APIs – Amoxicillin and Ampicillin.
note: The cut is done by an enzyme: since 1995 immobilised penicillin G acylase has been the industrial catalyst for large-scale hydrolysis of penicillin G to 6-APA (Frontiers in Bioengineering 2022, PMC9340067).

claim: Amoxicillin is the antibiotic in so many strips at home (VO L38)
source_quote: Amoxicillin-clavulanic acid 500/125mg tablet was the most consumed FDC (325 million DDDs, 6.4%).
note: Koya et al., Lancet Regional Health Southeast Asia 2022, India's private-sector antibiotic use in 2019. Framing supported.

claim: A bigger tank makes the powder cheaper: double the tank and the bill does not double, but output does; a big chakki grinds each kilo cheaper (VO L39, L41)
source_quote: For example, doubling capacity decreases the CoGs 1.4-fold (less, if many small bioreactors are used).
note: GEN, 15 Nov 2023. Doubling output while cost per kg falls 1.4 times means the total bill rises about 1.4 times, not 2. NITI June 2026: production is concentrated where there are economies of scale in fermentation. Note: power use itself grows roughly with tank size, so 'your costs don't double' is the safer word than 'bill' (optional). The chakki line is an analogy.

claim: The tank must stay clean, cool and full of air every hour, which takes a lot of power, water and steam (VO L40)
source_quote: In fermentation plants, the cost of utilities is an important component of costs.
note: ISID WP239: cold climate cuts fuel for chilled water in parts of China. MDPI 2021: Indian makers pay twice the rate on a per KWH basis for electricity and over 40 to 50% more for steam. News-Medical: the process runs aseptically and aerated.

claim: If even one stray germ gets in, you can lose the whole batch (VO L42)
source_quote: If a batch becomes contaminated, not only must the fermentation mixture (i.e. the yeast, feedstock, nutrients, water, etc.) be discarded, but the entire fermentation vessel must be emptied, cleaned, disinfected or sterilized as per the protocol of a production facility.
note: General fermentation practice (patent background on alcohol fermentation); penicillin runs are kept aseptic for the same reason (News-Medical).

claim: The country with the biggest tanks and the cheapest power wins (VO L43)
source_quote: Large-scale production facilities, favourable climatic conditions that lower energy requirements during certain stages of production, and government support through subsidised utilities and industrial infrastructure have enabled Chinese firms to achieve lower production costs.
note: Framing supported by NITI, ISID and CFR (scale plus cheap utilities).

claim: For years India's government allowed only a few companies to make penicillin, and only in small amounts, so the plants stayed too small to be cheap (VO L45)
source_quote: Till the early 2000s, the Government of India controlled the production of Pen-G in the country through licenses (Ghosh 2019). These licenses were given to a limited set of players, and for limited production capacities.
note: Same paragraph: the unit capacities at plant levels were sub-optimal to generate economies of scale. MDPI Economies 9:71 (2021), authors from ICMR, DoP, NPPA and CDSCO. ISID WP239: an industrial licensing policy that was not sensitive to domestic requirements; India's 1990 capacity (900 MMU) met only half of demand.

claim: In the 1990s China went all in on medicine ingredients (VO L46)
source_quote: The Chinese government’s support for the development of biotechnology in the 1990s led to the emergence of a fermentation based API industry in China.
note: RIS DP268: This has been the result of the implementation of a well- coordinated strategy in China (government invested in infrastructure, large-scale manufacturing, exports). MDPI: China strategically promoted its own API industry. ISID: China's Pen-G capacity went from 5,000-6,000 MMU (1990) to 160,000 MMU (2012).

claim: China built huge plants in huge parks with cheap power and water, and its factories faced looser pollution rules (VO L47)
source_quote: China offered more lax environmental laws, discounted water and power inputs, and, as more API and KSM manufacturing became sourced in that nation, enormous economies of scale.
note: RIS DP268: Large special economic zones and bulk drugs parks were set up with common utilities, common effluent treatment plants, uninterrupted power supply and steam, R&D facilities; Chinese SEZs are 10-15 times larger than in India. The sources say SEZs and bulk drug parks, so 'huge drug parks' is closer than 'chemical parks' (optional).

claim: Cheap Chinese penicillin flooded the world market at prices nobody else could match (VO L48)
source_quote: such as when China flooded the global market with low-priced penicillin and vitamin C in the early 2000s.
note: ISID WP239: China dumped Pen-G in India at costs below 40 percent of the actual cost of production, and the price of Pen-G crashed to $6/BU as compared to $24/BU (1985-2003). DGTR's 2010 preliminary findings also found dumping of Pen-G from China.

claim: In 1991, of all the medicine powder India bought from outside, China sold less than one per cent (VO L49-L50)
source_quote: In 1990 and 1991, India imported bulk drugs worth less than US $ 1 million and China’s share was less than 1 per cent (Annexure Table 1).
note: Sudip Chaudhuri, RIS Discussion Paper 268 (July 2021); Annex Table 1: 1991 imports from China US$0.40 mn = 0.3% share. ISID WP239: Imports from China accounted for less than one percent during that period (first half of the 1990s). On screen: UNDER 1% · 1991 [RIS 2021].

claim: Then, one by one, India's penicillin plants stopped: Hindustan Antibiotics, Alembic, Sarabhai, I.D.P.L., Torrent, Ranbaxy (VO L51-L54)
source_quote: After the removal of restrictions on the import of Pen-G, the domestic producers gradually withdrew from production – HAL (2003), JK and Torrent (2007), and Alembic (2011).
note: All six are listed as stopped in ISID Table 1, RIS Table 17 (Sarabhai, IDPL, Ranbaxy too) and MDPI Table 1. IDPL withdrew between 1998 and 2003 (ISID). A CAG audit (not opened, server error) reportedly dates HAL's stop to 1992. Alembic was the LAST to stop (2011); the roll call order is not a timeline, so show no years on the stamps, or end on Alembic.

claim: By the end of the 2010s India was importing all of its 6-APA, every last kilo (VO L55)
source_quote: By the end of 2010s, the entire requirement of 6-APA was met by imports.
note: DGTR 6-APA anti-dumping initiation of 25 Sep 2026 (Corpseed summary): the applicant Qule Pharma started production in FY 2024-25 and earlier Indian 6-APA manufacturing had stopped. CFR June 2026: China controls about 94 percent of 6-APA.

claim: Niti Aayog says Chinese powder costs thirty-five to forty per cent less than powder made in India (VO L57)
source_quote: APIs imported from China are estimated to be 35–40% cheaper than domestically produced alternatives
note: Keep it attributed to Niti Aayog (optional: Niti Aayog estimates). NITI cites ISID WP239, which takes the figure from Bart, Aggarwal and Singh (2013) and KPMG-CII (2020), so it is an old estimate. On screen: 35-40% CHEAPER [NITI AAYOG ESTIMATE].

claim: For about thirty years that trap held, then 2020 (VO L59)
source_quote: However, towards the end of 1990s the share of China in India’s import of APIs increased to more than 20 percent and reached 57 percent by 2010 (Figure 1).
note: Framing: from under 1% (1991) to the 2020 shock is about thirty years.

claim: In 2020 the central government launched a scheme paying companies extra to make forty-one missing ingredients in India, with nearly seven thousand crore rupees set aside (VO L60-L61)
source_quote: with a total financial outlay of ₹6,940 crore. A total of 258 applications were received under the Scheme for 41 products across four target segments
note: MDPI 2021: In March 2020 the Union Cabinet, chaired by the prime minister, approved the following schemes (bulk drug parks and the PLI). The incentive is paid on sales (20% for fermentation products, 10% for chemical ones). On screen: 41 INGREDIENTS · ₹6,940 CRORE.

claim: One company took the biggest bet of all (VO L62)
source_quote: Lyfius Pharma Pvt. Ltd.- 1,910 Penicillin G Kakinada Andhra Pradesh
note: DoP table of commissioned projects (investment in crore rupees). Rs 1,910 crore out of Rs 4,763 crore total actual investment (Sept 2025) is the largest single project (our inference: the next named one is Kinvan at Rs 450 crore, and the segment totals leave no room for a bigger one).

claim: Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, on the coast: the plant was built by Lyfius, a unit of Aurobindo Pharma (VO L63)
source_quote: Lyfius Pharma Private Limited, a wholly owned step-down subsidiary of the Company
note: Plant address in the release: A.V. Nagaram (V), kakinada SEZ area, Thondangi (M), Kakinada District. Kakinada is situated along the Bay of Bengal, and a greenfield seaport is planned in the Kakinada SEZ (Wikipedia, Kakinada). Business Today 1 Apr 2024: located in a SEZ at Kakinada.

claim: Inside are giant tanks (VO L64)
source_quote: This is one of the largest fermentation-based antibiotic intermediates plant in India with cutting edge technology including high-volume fermenters
note: Company description. No source gives the fermenter sizes, so draw no scale numbers in the 3D shot.

claim: The company says the plant cost around two thousand five hundred crore rupees (replacement for VO L64)
source_quote: Under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, Lyfius Pharma Private Limited (Lyfius Pharma) invested ₹2,500 crores in Penicillin-G (Pen-G) facility
note: REPLACES L64 'It cost around two thousand five hundred crore rupees' (say it is the company's figure). Other figures: Business Today/PTI 1 Apr 2024: The Rs 2,400 crore Pen-G plant; DoP Annual Report 2025-26 lists the PLI investment as Rs 1,910 crore. Put the other figures in notes, not on screen.

claim: The plant is built to make fifteen thousand tonnes of penicillin G every year (VO L64)
source_quote: With an annual production capacity of 15,000 metric tonnes (MT)
note: Business Today 1 Apr 2024: has a production capacity of 15,000 tonne per annum. GKToday (11 Oct 2026): stated capacity of 15,000 tonnes. It is capacity, not output, which the VO's 'built to make' gets right.

claim: In 2024 the tanks started running (VO L65)
source_quote: Commercial production to ramp up in FY25
note: Business Today 1 Apr 2024: Aurobindo said it had commissioned the plant; trial production was expected in April 2024. DGTR anti-dumping initiation (28 Sep 2026, WorldTradeScanner summary): The applicant started production in FY 2024-25. The PM inaugurated it on 29 Oct 2024. A fire in the coal-crusher area halted it from April to 29 June 2025.

claim: For the first time in more than ten years, India is growing its own penicillin again (replacement for VO L65; same fix for L75)
source_quote: As per evidence available, petitioners’ production accounts for 100% of the Indian production of Penicillin- G.
note: REPLACES L65 'For the first time in about thirty years'. DGTR preliminary findings (11 Feb 2010): Alembic (Vadodara) and SPIC were making Pen-G in India in 2005-2009 (investigation period Oct 2008 to Mar 2009). ISID WP239: Alembic withdrew in 2011. MDPI 2021: India had significant domestic production of both Pen-G and 6-APA in the late 1990s and mid-2000s. So the gap before Kakinada (FY 2024-25) was about 13 years. Claims of a 30-year gap (GKToday 11 Oct 2026: a hiatus dating to the late 1980s; a UPSC site) are contradicted by this record. The company's own release makes no such claim.

claim: Even with Indian penicillin ready, cheap imports were waiting at the port (VO L66)
source_quote: International price for Pen-G had fallen to $13.5 a kg by late 2025
note: Moneycontrol (Jan 2026): the $25 level analysts estimate is required for domestic production to remain profitable. CFR June 2026: Chinese producers recently flooded the market with below-cost exports of APIs and KSMs to cripple alternative suppliers in India that were supported under India’s Production-Linked Incentive scheme.

claim: On the twenty-ninth of January 2026 the government stepped in (replacement for VO L67)
source_quote: Notification No. 56/2025-26 New Delhi, Dated: 29th January, 2026
note: REPLACES L67 'the government did something it rarely does'. Not rare: DGFT had already set a minimum import price on sulfadiazine API (Notification 41/2025-26, 10 Oct 2025, Rs 1,774/kg; extended to 30 Nov 2026 by Notification 40/2026-27 of 30 Sep 2026) and one on ATS-8 (US$111/kg). Drishti IAS (3 Feb 2026) says the Pen-G floor builds on those earlier steps.

claim: A minimum price at the border: penicillin G cheaper than about two thousand two hundred rupees a kilo now can't come into India without a special licence; amoxicillin and 6-APA got minimum prices too (replacement for VO L68)
source_quote: (a) However, import of Penicillin G-potassium (PEN-G) having CIF value less than INR 2,216/- per Kilogram is ‘Restricted’.
note: REPLACES L68 'Penicillin G cannot come into India cheaper than about two thousand two hundred rupees a kilo'. Restricted = allowed only with a DGFT import authorisation, and 100% EOUs, SEZ units and Advance Authorisation imports are exempt if not sold in India, so 'cannot come in' overstates. Other floors in the same notification: amoxicillin trihydrate Rs 2,733/kg, 6-APA Rs 3,405/kg (CIF). Copy of the signed DGFT notification hosted by LiveLaw; gazette S.O. 429(E). On screen: ₹2,216/KG (CIF).
